title: Secret scanning in the repository and in the Git history

videos.script: Your project has had a password in it since its first day. It is linkbox's administration token, written into the settings file. {{token}} Deleting that line feels like the fix. It is not. Every commit is a full snapshot of the project, and every clone keeps every commit. {{copies}} So a secret that was committed has been published, to everybody who could ever read the repository. The response starts somewhere else. The value has to stop working. {{revoke}} In this lesson you scan the files and the whole history with gitleaks, and find the token in your first commit. You move it out of the code and rotate it, and you watch the service refuse the old value. {{rotate}} Then you decide what to do about the history, and why rewriting it comes last, if it comes at all. {{history}} Last, two checks keep the next one out. A hook refuses the commit on your laptop. And a stage in the pipeline reads the whole history on every push, before anything else runs. {{pipeline}}
